name: Building the Teacher to Strengthen Numeracy in Primary Schools

content.text: The Project is a joint collaboration between four universities: Aga Khan University's Institute for Educational Development in East Africa, Tshwane University of Technology and Cape Peninsula University of Technology in South Africa and The Oxford University UK who were the overall lead in the project.

The focus of AFLA research project was to generate new knowledge about how to develop and sustain teacher capacity and skills in effective integration and use of assessment for improving learning outcomes in numeracy in particular in challenging educational settings.

Altogether, the four university project partners, along with invited high-level government representatives as well as several external experts and teachers from across the region, discussed the current state of the AFLA research project and planned future activities.

In the workshop, the project partners presented an analysis of the present situation of the study. Participants of the study included 500 pupils from 6 purposively selected schools from one informal urban settlement in Dar es Salaam.  Selected mathematics teachers, head teachers and relevant stakeholders from the ward and zone level of education administration were also included. It was generally expected that the research would provide insights into how teachers can raise the standards of their teaching through the practice of assessing classroom learning; and how teachers can help students know where they are in learning.

Speaking during the Workshop, Prof. Therese Hopfenbeck said "Assessment for learning principles must be influenced by the relevance of the context in which it is implemented.  Moving forward from this dissemination, we must take a research perspective from the analysis of data to critically assess the outcomes and how we will use the research to engage with local communities."

One of the key emerging findings highlighted by Prof. Anjum Halai "Group learning for students has been an effective strategy for learning and peer to peer support. The strategy has been used as a management tool that has divided students into different levels of learning and has established a practice of support amongst groups for learning. There are conceptual issues in mathematics that need to be focused on. Teachers are understanding that answers are important but equally important are the competencies and processes of getting to the answers. AFLA shifts the onus of learning on the learner; teachers have to enable learning and allow students to be the owners of their learning. Teachers need to release control to let learners be learners"

The vivid discussions were enriched by short presentations of some of the research stakeholders and partners sharing their experiences in relation to research collaboration, capacity building and mobility. Such mechanisms could be taken as an example for good international collaboration and might help to distribute the idea and outcome of the AFLA research project, as was stated in the lively discussion after the presentations. Project partners and all stakeholders showed enthusiasm and elation regarding the future project development.

content.title: Building the Teacher to Strengthen Numeracy in Primary Schools
content.author: sabrina zahor
content.description: On this day, 45 participants from the Local government schools and teacher educators attended a one day workshop to disseminate emerging findings of its Assessment for Learning (AFLA) Research Project. AFLA launched in 2016; Implemented in Tanzania and South Africa, the project aims to raise the numeracy competence standards of school children. The three year project has been working with teachers to raise the standards of teaching numeracy in primary schools through effective classroom based assessment.
